依存図のアプリのスワイプで余白が見えないようにする

## 変更

依存図のアプリ (agent-tasks) で、端を越えてスワイプすると窓やスクロール領域が跳ね返り、背景の余白が見えていた。
macOS の WKWebView の既定の動きなので、`style.css` の全要素に `overscroll-behavior: none` を置いて止める。
このプロパティは継承されないため、窓、依存図、右の列、メモの一覧、単体ビューをまとめて覆えるよう全称セレクタにした。

## 検証

- `task gui:test`: go vet、gosec、go test、フロントエンドの 127 件がすべて通過
- 追加したテストが修正前に落ちることを確認
- `task gui:build` で建てたアプリを実機で起動し、スワイプの挙動を確認

## 残した課題

- 跳ね返りは WKWebView の描画でしか起きず happy-dom では再現できないので、自動テストは CSS の規則の有無だけを確かめる

fix(tool): skip the seatbelt probe when a nested sandbox refuses it

## What changed

- **`tool/confinement_darwin.go`**: `seatbeltProbe` now answers with three facts — usable, whether the process
  could be **started**, and the applier's own `stderr` — and `probeSeatbelt` stays the bool wrapper the
  availability probe uses.
- **`tool/confinement_darwin_test.go`**: the probe test **skips** when the applier could not be spawned because
  this process is confined (`operation not permitted`), printing the command and its stderr; it still **fails**
  when the applier ran and refused, or failed for any other reason.

## Why the distinction matters

A nested sandbox (this agent's `workspace-write` policy) says nothing about the host's capability, so failing
there is a false alarm — and the same test passing in CI cannot see it. But a `sandbox-exec` that *runs* and
then refuses its target **is** a broken host, and must not be softened into a skip. The classifier is a
one-line predicate, `nestedSandboxRefusal(spawnFailed, reason)`, with a table test; dropping the `spawnFailed`
half fails it on the "applier ran and refused" case.

## A negative control that proved nothing

Growing the `/bin/false` assertion exposed that macOS has no `/bin/false`: the probe had been answering
"unusable" for a **missing file**, so the control never exercised a binary that runs and exits non-zero. It now
resolves `false` on `PATH` and requires the probe to have spawned it.

## Verification

| Where | Command | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| unconfined (this host) | `go test ./tool -run 'TestProbeSeatbeltIsASmokeRun\|TestNestedSandboxRefusalClassifies\|TestSeatbeltBoundaryIsEnforced'` | all pass; the boundary test still enforces its three cases |
| nested refusal (reproduction) | `sandbox-exec -p '(deny process-exec (literal "/usr/bin/sandbox-exec"))' … -test.run TestProbeSeatbeltIsASmokeRun` | **SKIP** with `fork/exec /usr/bin/sandbox-exec: operation not permitted` |
| broken applier (reproduction) | `sandbox-exec -p '(deny process-exec (literal "/usr/bin/true"))' …` | **FAIL** with `exit status 71: sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted` — a broken host is still caught |
| nested, whole package | `cd tool && sandbox-exec -p '…' go test . -count=1` | `ok … 29.5s`; the probe and boundary tests skip, nothing else is affected |

- `go test ./... -count=1` → 18 packages `ok`; `go test ./tool -race` → `ok`; `go vet` (darwin and linux),
  `gofmt -l` clean; test count 1414 → 1415.
- `git log --format='%h %G? %s'` → `G`, on `fix/seatbelt-nested-probe`.

## Honest scope

- **The reproduction is a profile I wrote**, not the DSH `workspace-write` policy itself: this session runs with
  `danger-full-access`, so the original failure cannot be produced in-place. The profile denies exactly the
  spawn the issue describes, and the captured message matches the issue's screenshot of the failure.
- The skip is still a skip: in a nested sandbox the host's seatbelt capability is **not** verified. The test
  says so in the skip line rather than passing silently.

fix: history table unreadable when plugin and Unraid colour schemes differ

Closes #270

The cells of the "Show as table" view under Fans > History took their text colour from Unraid's table styles. With the plugin dark on a light Unraid theme (or the reverse) the text matched the card background. The cells and caption now use the plugin's colour variables and ignore host backgrounds, the same approach as `.unc-table` (#91). The feedback diag preview (`pre`) gets an explicit text colour as well. The other tables (profiles, probe) already use `.unc-table`.

New e2e scenario `host-theme-contrast` emulates a light and a dark Unraid theme, opens the table in both mixed combinations and asserts contrast of at least 4.5:1 (before: 1.01:1 and 1.12:1; after: 5.71:1 and 5.85:1).

fix: 依存図のポップアップの「セッション終了」の丸を灰で出す

Closes #447

## 変更

- 依存図の単体ビュー (ポップアップ) で、終了したセッションの状態の chip の丸が作業中と同じ緑で出ていた。
  原因は `.dot` の既定の背景が緑で、色の規則の無い `exited` が作業中と同じ色になったこと。
- `.dot` の既定を `.st` と同じ灰にし、緑は `working` の鍵で明示する (状態の chip、daemon が動いている footer、open のメモ)。
  `.dot.off` は既定と同じになるので消す。
- 色の規則を `:is(.dot, .st).<tone>` の 1 組にまとめ、`.dot` と `.st` の片方だけに書き忘れることを CSS の形で起こせなくする。

## 検証

- 足したテストは修正前に落ち、修正後に通る。`STATE_TONE` の色すべてに共有の規則があること、形ごとの色の規則が無いこと、
  既定が灰であること、丸の class が状態の色の鍵を持つことを確かめる。
- `npm --prefix gui/frontend test`: 110 件すべて pass (main を取り込んだ後)。

## 残した課題

- `STATE_TONE` (JS) に足した色の鍵に CSS の規則があることは、言語機能では結べずテストで確かめている。書き忘れても丸は灰で出る。
- 実際のアプリの画面では色を確かめていない。確かめたのは `style.css` の規則と丸の class まで。

fix(office): keep ROUND caches finite at extreme scales

ROUND could cache NaN when its decimal scale became infinity or zero, and infinity when an intermediate overflowed despite a finite rounded result. Bound extreme digit counts and split large positive scales so tiny numbers still round correctly. Preserve finite results; emit #NUM! only when the rounded result itself overflows.

Fixes #1335

Validation: 37 generated-XLSX cases inspect the cached value and formula. Before the fix, 23 fail and 14 controls pass; all pass after. Controls cover positive/negative subnormal inputs, large finite results, scale boundaries, 15-digit ties, ordinary negative/zero/fractional digit counts, text coercion and IFERROR. The complete office package passes with `-race`; package vet, both doc-path suites and privacy checks pass.

No spreadsheet application or Docker/service integration was qualified locally. No UI changes are included.

+++ b/docs/lessons/server.md
@@ -935,6 +935,10 @@ A verified download or unpacked binary is still temporary until its final rename
 
 `strconv.ParseFloat` accepts `NaN` and infinity without an error. Reject them when coercing formula text so existing `#VALUE!` and `IFERROR` behavior works instead of caching non-finite numbers. Verify generated workbook values, with numeric text, range references and lazy branches as controls.
 
+## Decimal rounding scales can overflow before the result does (#1335)
+
+`ROUND` can have a finite result even when its power of ten or scaled intermediate overflows. Bound places by the float64 range, split large positive scales for tiny inputs, and retain numbers whose rounding place is already below their precision. Only a genuinely overflowing rounded result becomes `#NUM!`. Test emitted XLSX caches, including subnormal values, large finite results, 15-digit ties and `IFERROR`.
+
 ## Database passwords need URI userinfo encoding (#6160)
 
 Query escaping turns spaces into plus signs, but URI userinfo decoding keeps a plus literal. Build credentials with `url.UserPassword`, and check the generated database URL with the actual driver's parser. Comparing a provisioning result against the same URL helper cannot detect this password change.

+package office

+func TestRoundCachedValues(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct{ formula, want string }{
+		{"ROUND(1.25,309)", "1.25"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25,-400)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(-1.25,309)", "-1.25"},
+		{"ROUND(-1.25,-400)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(0,309)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(0,-400)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25,1e100)", "1.25"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25,-1e100)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(1e300,20)", "1e300"},
+		{"ROUND(-1e300,20)", "-1e300"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25e-309,309)", "1e-309"},
+		{"ROUND(-1.25e-309,309)", "-1e-309"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25e-310,309)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(1e-320,309)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(-1e-320,309)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(2.5e-309,309)", "3e-309"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25e-320,320)", "1e-320"},
+		{"ROUND(5e-324,323)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(5e-324,324)", "5e-324"},
+		{"ROUND(1.25,308)", "1.25"},
+		{"ROUND(5e307,-308)", "1e308"},
+		{"ROUND(1.7e308,-309)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(1.7e308,-308)", "#NUM!"},
+		{"IFERROR(ROUND(1.7e308,-308),7)", "7"},
+		{"IFERROR(ROUND(1.25,309),7)", "1.25"},
+		{"IFERROR(ROUND(1.25,-400),7)", "0"},
+		{"ROUND(2.345,2)", "2.35"},
+		{"ROUND(2.3449999999999998,2)", "2.35"},
+		{"ROUND(-1.475,2)", "-1.48"},
+		{"ROUND(21.5,-1)", "20"},
+		{"ROUND(626.3,-3)", "1000"},
+		{"ROUND(2.5,0)", "3"},
+		{"ROUND(-2.5,0)", "-3"},
+		{"ROUND(1.234,2.9)", "1.23"},
+		{`ROUND("1.25",2)`, "1.25"},
+		{`ROUND("NaN",2)`, "#VALUE!"},
+		{`IFERROR(ROUND("bad",2),7)`, "7"},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.formula, func(t *testing.T) {
+			src, err := json.Marshal(workbookSpec{Sheets: []sheetSpec{{Rows: [][]any{{"=" + tc.formula}}}}})
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			data, err := Xlsx(src, "")
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			var sheet struct {
+				Cell struct {
+					Type    string `xml:"t,attr"`
+					Formula string `xml:"f"`
+					Value   string `xml:"v"`
+				} `xml:"sheetData>row>c"`
+			}
+			if err := xml.Unmarshal([]byte(parts(t, data)["xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml"]), &sheet); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			c := sheet.Cell
+			if c.Formula != tc.formula {
+				t.Fatalf("cached formula %q, want %q", c.Formula, tc.formula)
+			}
+			if strings.HasPrefix(tc.want, "#") {
+				if c.Type != "e" || c.Value != tc.want {
+					t.Fatalf("cache type %q value %q, want error %s", c.Type, c.Value, tc.want)

+			got, err := strconv.ParseFloat(c.Value, 64)
+			want, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(tc.want, 64)
+			// The writer stores 15 significant digits; subnormal results also have a float64 quantum.
+			tolerance := math.Max(math.Abs(want)*1e-14, math.SmallestNonzeroFloat64)
+			if math.Abs(want) == math.SmallestNonzeroFloat64 {
+				tolerance = 0 // preserving the smallest nonzero value must not accept zero
+			}
+			if c.Type != "" || err != nil || math.IsNaN(got) || math.IsInf(got, 0) ||
+				want == 0 && got != 0 || math.Abs(got-want) > tolerance {
+				t.Fatalf("cache type %q value %q, want finite %s", c.Type, c.Value, tc.want)
+			}
+		})
+	}

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(transaction): recreate pruned lock state directory

## Summary

Fix a lock acquisition race exposed after #182 merged: a concurrent release can prune `.scbake` after another process resolves the lock paths, causing acquisition to fail with:

```text
invalid lock path: lstat .../.scbake: no such file or directory
```

This was the Ubuntu/Go 1.27 failure on #181 and can affect any first acquisition after release prunes the state directory.

## Details

- `resolveRootLockPaths` no longer resolves the state directory or lock file before they exist.
- `ensureRootLockDir` creates `.scbake`, then validates containment.
- The lock file is still opened through the safe helpers, and path revalidation still runs after acquisition.
- Added a regression test that resolves paths before `.scbake` exists and acquires successfully.

## Tests

- [x] Existing tests pass (`go test ./...`)
- [x] New regression test added

`go test ./... -count=1`, `golangci-lint run --timeout=5m ./...`, and the focused lock test pass.

## API Impact

- [x] No public API changes
- [ ] Backward-compatible API change
- [ ] Breaking API change

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project standards and idiomatic Go
- [x] `golangci-lint` passes
- [x] Public APIs are documented where applicable
- [x] Commit history is focused

## Related Issues

- Refs #133, lock remains open for the deferred rollback content-hash check.

AI assistance is disclosed in the commit trailers (`Assisted-by: OpenCode (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash)`).

Reject Bitbucket webhooks whose repository full name has no owner

A Bitbucket push or pull request webhook whose `repository.full_name` has no slash panics the hook handler: `convertRepo` splits that field and reads element 1. An empty JSON body is enough, since the field then decodes to the empty string. The router recovers the panic, so the caller sees a 500 where a malformed payload should give a 400.

Gitea and Forgejo already check for the separator in `validate()` before converting. This does the same for Bitbucket and returns an incomplete payload error instead. `convertRepo` now uses `strings.Cut` so the API callers cannot reach that index either. Two cases added to `TestParseHook`; both panic on main.

Validation: `go test -race -count=1 ./server/forge/bitbucket/...`, with `golangci-lint` v2.15.0 and `gofumpt -extra` clean on the package.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and its tests.

fix(install): find the newest release while every release is a pre-release

Without `ARMADA_VERSION`, `install.sh` asked GitHub for `releases/latest`, which leaves out pre-releases. Every Armada release is a pre-release so far, so the one-line install (`curl ... | sudo sh -s - init`) stopped with "could not determine the latest release".

It now falls back to the newest published release when `releases/latest` has none. Checked against GitHub: with no version set it installs `v0.1.0-alpha.2`. The one-line commands that `armada token create` prints pin the version and were not affected.
